title: Mechanics Instruction that Sticks: Using Simple Warm-Ups to Improve Student Writing
author: Stuart Jr., Dave
summary: This article introduces Doug Stark's systematic warm-up approach to grammar and mechanics instruction, which Stuart describes as the most effective approach to language conventions instruction he has encountered in his classroom career. Guest author Doug Stark recounts the failure of two conventional approaches — unfocused free writing that neglected conventions, and an intensive six-week grammar boot camp that produced diagram-able sentences but no lasting writing transfer. The breakthrough came when Stark adopted the John Collins writing approach and later developed his own sequence of daily five-minute warm-ups that embed grammar instruction in authentic writing contexts across the full school year. Stark's method is built on three principles: repetition until automaticity, immediate transfer to real writing tasks, and sequenced difficulty across 13 thematic units per level. Stuart notes that standardized test results showed striking improvement among students who had worked through Stark's warm-up sequence, though Stark is careful to point out that test preparation is not the purpose — authentic writing growth is.
points: Six-week grammar boot camps produce students who can diagram sentences but not write better — true learning requires repeated practice embedded in authentic writing across the whole year
Stark's warm-up method is built on automaticity through repetition: John Wooden's principle that 'the importance of repetition until automaticity cannot be overstated' guides the sequence
The warm-up format (short, daily, sequenced, tied to real writing) allows grammar instruction to compound without crowding out time for actual writing practice
Upper-level teachers could identify students who had worked through Stark's program by their visible command of English conventions — a rare, concrete outcome measure
The four-level structure (13 units per level, plus quizzes and supplemental activities) allows teachers to meet students where they are and advance them systematically
